rejected.finding: The dataset was 1 million public Twitter posts from 2010
rejected.reason: Both releases say 'collected in 2010'. The paper says 'The dataset was collected in 2023' and its footnote cites huggingface enryu43/twitter100m_tweets with data 'in 2021-2023'. The primary source contradicts 2010, so 2010 is not carried. The 1 million count is carried from the paper (c16) and the paper's year is carried as the paper's statement (c17).

rejected.finding: Control posts had 500 or fewer likes, retweets or replies and more than 100 tokens (release wording)
rejected.reason: The release says '500 or fewer likes, retweets or replies'. The paper says control samples had 'a popularity of = 0 =0' and a token length over 100. Use the paper's definition in c18.

rejected.finding: The four models included 'Qwen3 4B Instruct' (release model list)
rejected.reason: The paper names the fourth model 'Qwen3 4B Thinking 2507'. The release's model list is not carried, and c25 uses the paper's names.

rejected.finding: Three graduate students validated the GPT-4o mini labels
rejected.reason: The release and the paper's main text say graduate students ('three graduate student annotators'). Appendix B describes the same annotators as 'three human experts (junior, senior, and postdoctoral researchers)'. The paper contradicts itself, so only 'three human annotators' is carried (c24).

rejected.finding: UT Austin and Purdue co-authors (which authors are at which institution)
rejected.reason: The paper lists Texas A&M University, University of Texas at Austin and Purdue University as one block under the author list and never maps authors to institutions. The funding note ties J. Hong and Z. Wang to a UT Austin grant (c9), and one corresponding address is jyhong@nus.edu.sg. No single author is placed at UT Austin or Purdue in the record.

rejected.finding: Tu led or designed the study (the releases' framing 'Research by Dr. Zhengzhong Tu and his colleagues')
rejected.reason: The paper's contribution statement credits Z. Wang with the original idea (c7), J. Hong with designing the experiments with S. Xing, and Z. Tu and A. Grama with 'writing suggestions and computational resource support' (c8). That Tu is on the paper and quoted is verified. That he led the design is not stated by the paper.

rejected.finding: Ext-Reflect healed the model or restored its accuracy after 6 iterations
rejected.reason: The paper says only that Ext-Reflect 'converges to a thought-skipping rate similar to the baseline' and that 'the decline can be largely reduced'. The text reports no accuracy figure for it. Only the thought-skipping claim is carried (c49).

rejected.finding: Personality figures from Table 2, for example psychopathy rising to 75.7
rejected.reason: Table 2 shows control-only training already moved these scores far from Base (psychopathy Base 2.2, M1 0% junk 39.7). The paper says continual pre-training's 'impacts on personalities are non-trivial but inconsistent'. Table-level personality numbers would overstate the junk effect, so only the paper's own trait statements are carried (c54 to c56).
